title: The multi-agent workflow
request: Put the measured roles to work together on the workflow graph: each passed what the earlier steps produced, under the graph validator, with a person approving the gates, within a budget, and the person asked only what the roles could not settle.
spec: The roles placed on the workflow graph's nodes (WF-01 to WF-10), passed the artefacts of the earlier nodes, under the graph validator, with a person's approval at the gates, budgets per project, and the conversation as the front that asks the person what only they can say. Done when the fraud replica and a churn and a regression replica run end to end with all roles on, every move validated and traced, within a set budget, and the person asked only what the roles could not settle.
plan: Write one team runner that calls each role at its step with the artefacts of the steps before: brief, findings, plan, programs, stage records, report.
Require both gates and let only the person sign them; every other write a validated move.
Share one capped advisor among the roles and the critic; switch the stage notes' model off inside a run.
Fix a gate before the run: completion, validated moves, the person asked only the open fields, the holdout once, the cap, every role asked, and each kind's acceptance decisions still reached.
Review, fix, dry-run with a scripted advisor, then run live once under the owner's cap.

decisions.decision: The roles must not leave the solution worse than the rules: each replica must still reach its kind's acceptance decisions.
decisions.why: A team that answers more but decides worse is not progress; the kinds' acceptance (16.2) is the measure of deciding well.

decisions.decision: The feature programs are proposed before the person signs the solution, and shown to them.
decisions.why: They change what the features stage computes; a signature that does not cover them is not a signature.

decisions.decision: The critic is the run's only (a context-scoped advisor), never left switched on.
decisions.why: It failed its own gate (18.6); a setting left on would bring an uncapped critic to later runs.

change: dclab_rnd/studio/team.py (Person, run, the steps WF-01 to WF-10), engine.advisor_scope as a context variable, agent.notes_off, the capped GatewayAdvisor re-reading its cap before each request and counting calls, intern set_solution accepting a label file's target, dclab_core plan choosing a time split for rows ordered in time, provisional rows taken from the earliest 80% when time orders them, the harness dclab_rnd/agent_eval/team.py with team_gate_v1, tests/test_team.py.

findings.defect: The intern's set_solution refused a solution whose target comes from a label file.
findings.scenario: On the fraud replica, set_solution raised 'Column is_fraud is not in the data': the data file has no is_fraud; the label file defines it.
findings.cause: The column check read the data file's columns only.
findings.fix: The label file's target counts as a column of the joined table.
findings.impact: No project with a label file could get a solution through the intern or the team.

findings.defect: The plan chose a random split for rows that arrive over time.
findings.scenario: On the churn replica, signups over two years with a rising cancel rate: the plan's split was stratified because no drift was measured, so the holdout mixed early and late signups.
findings.cause: The time split was chosen only when drift was measured; a sample this size can miss it.
findings.fix: Rows ordered in time get a time split (DCLAB-R02), drift measured or not; a random split only when no time orders them.
findings.test: the binary kind's acceptance through the team; test_core_plan
findings.impact: Scores on such tables were optimistic about the future the model meets.

findings.defect: The live run would have sent up to 30 uncapped, uncounted model requests.
findings.scenario: Every stage's notes went through the installed gateway's stage_notes purpose, outside the team's cap and spend.
findings.cause: Only the critic and the roles used the team's advisor.
findings.fix: Stage notes ask no model inside a team run (notes_off); the reporter is the team's prose.
findings.impact: The euro cap would not have bounded the run.

findings.defect: The gate could pass with a single role answering.
findings.scenario: A scripted run where only the reporter answered got pass 'with every role on'.
findings.cause: The verdict only asked that some role answered.
findings.fix: Every role must be asked on every replica (counted per purpose), every needs_approval move must be followed by its approval, and the kind's baselines check is added back.

findings.defect: The person was asked what was already settled, and their answers were thrown away.
findings.scenario: The analyst's open question used field 'target' and the essential 'target_column', so the target was asked twice; answers never reached the brief, so the plan said the moment was 'assumed, not stated'.
findings.cause: Field names differed and answers went only into a log.
findings.fix: Aliases map the fields, settled fields are skipped, and every answer is written into the brief the later roles read.

findings.defect: Project writes bypassed the graph validator, and the critic stayed on.
findings.scenario: Pack, programs, policy and settings were saved directly; settings.critic stayed true, so a later models run built an uncapped critic that had failed its gate.
findings.cause: Writes were made as plain saves.
findings.fix: Each write is a validated, logged set_settings move; programs come before the signature; the critic is scoped to the run.

findings.defect: The advisor scope was a process-wide global.
findings.scenario: A worker thread running another project's models stage during a team run would have used the team's advisor and cap.
findings.cause: A module global, documented as not thread-shared.

findings.defect: The euro cap was not a hard bound across purposes and replicas.
findings.scenario: Each purpose's client got its limit once, at creation; a client from replica 1 kept its full limit through replicas 2 and 3.
findings.cause: The limit was set when the client was made.
findings.fix: The advisor re-reads the shared cap before every request.

findings.defect: A failing stage aborted the run and lost the record.
findings.scenario: A GraphBlocked or a stage error escaped team.run, and measure() stored nothing after paid requests.
findings.cause: No catch per stage or per replica.
findings.fix: team.run returns a stopped status with where and why; measure() stores a failed replica's row.

findings.defect: The trace under-reported what roles added and dropped what they refused.
findings.scenario: An entity the investigator proposed showed as 'rules'; the planner said 'advisor' when it kept nothing; refusals were not stored.
findings.cause: Sources were guessed from whether an advisor existed.
findings.fix: The investigator's contribution is the findings it added over a rules-only analysis; each step stores kept, refused and the reason.

findings.defect: A scripted approval was recorded as the owner's.
findings.scenario: approve_gate always wrote by='owner' even when the approval came from a lambda in the harness.
findings.fix: Person.who is recorded with each approval; the harness says 'scripted person'.

findings.defect: Assertions were vacuous and new paths untested.
findings.scenario: An assertion ended in 'or q["field"]'; nothing showed the critic used the team's advisor, a holdout decline, or the cap.
findings.cause: Tests written for the happy path.
findings.fix: Tests for the critic's requests, the asked fields, the holdout decline, a private project with the critic on, and the cap.

findings.defect: The review budget was misread or lost.
findings.scenario: '0.5' became half the rows; '.5%' became 5%; '70 a day' was dropped.
findings.cause: A loose percent pattern and no span of days.
findings.fix: The percent pattern reads .5%; a bare number is a share only below 0.05; a count a day uses the rows' span; one re-ask.

findings.defect: The person's target was matched only by exact name.
findings.scenario: 'the churned column' stopped the run at WF-01.
findings.fix: Case-insensitive, or the one column named in the words; one re-ask with the options.

findings.defect: The plan's analysis read rows the time-based holdout would hold.
findings.scenario: On the churn replica, a seeded random 80% of rows informed the forbidden and grouping decisions, although the holdout is the latest signups.
findings.fix: With a time column, the provisional rows are the earliest 80%.

measurements.name: team on three replicas, live (TEAM-001)
measurements.gate: team_gate_v1, fixed before the run: each run completes; every move allowed or waiting for an approval that then comes; the person asked at most the two essentials, the budget and three open questions; every role asked on every replica; the holdout read once; the spend under the cap; each replica still reaches its kind's acceptance decisions.
measurements.result: All 3 completed with every role asked, moves validated, gates signed, the holdout read once, EUR 0.0084 under the EUR 0.5 cap. Fraud and delivery reached every acceptance decision; on churn the planner chose average precision where the binary kind expects ROC-AUC.
measurements.against_gate: Completion, validated moves, questions, every role asked, the holdout and the cap all hold on all 3 replicas; the acceptance decisions hold on fraud and delivery but not on churn, where the metric is not ROC-AUC, so the gate fails.
limits: One run with one model; the planner's metric choice may differ on another run.
Replicas and a scripted person, not a real project or a real conversation.
measurements.next: Keep the roles off by default; let 18.9 decide each role on its own gate, and look at when the planner may change the primary metric.

outcome: Built and measured: the roles work together under the validator, the gates and one budget; the live run failed its gate on one decision (the planner's metric on churn), and two product gaps found on the way were fixed.
lessons: A team run is where single-role measurements meet: a role that passed alone can still change a decision the whole must keep.
Count every request a run makes, not only the ones you meant: stage notes were outside the cap.
Fix the dry-run's failures in the product, not in the gate: the time-split rule was a real gap.
risks: A role's answer silently overriding a person's or the rules' decision.
The trace claiming a model's contribution that never happened.
A failure mid-run losing what was spent.
